newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. weakened slightly Thursday, but the market was described as quiet with many players away from their offices to attend an industry function in Houston.
"The market came down a bit today and on Wednesday," said one trade source. "But there is very little going on."
Daily prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were assessed at $14.50-15.00 per megwatt hour (MWh), down from $15.00-15.50 on Wednesday.
Next-day electricity at California's Midway substation was quoted $17.50-18.00.

The Portland, Ore.-based Bonneville Power Administration continued to offer power during heavy load hours at $17.00, but did limit firm volumes to 200 MW. BPA also offered expansion power to Northwest and Southwest buyers during off-peak hours at $9.00.
"The Bonneville offers didn't really affect the market today," said a California trader. "There isn't that much interest at those prices."
Southwest prices also fell today, with on-peak Palo Verde cited at $21.00 per MWh, compared with $22.00 on Wednesday.
"Prices are receding a bit," said an Arizona trader. "Laramie (Platte River Authority's coal plant) is back up and loads are declining."
Others noted that the resumption of recently-interrupted gas shipments on the El Paso pipeline will likely put downward pressure on San Juan gas prices, which should cap Southwest electricity prices.
Cash October prices for COB were cited at $15.50-16.00, down from $15.90-16.35 on Wednesday. Palo Verde for October was quoted $15.75-16.25, down from $16.25-17.00.
"It's been hard to get a hold of anybody this week, that's why the spreads are so big," noted a broker.
